India Rejects US Tariff Pressure, Cites National Interest in Energy Policy

#India-US Relations #Russian Oil #Kirti Vardhan Singh #Sanctions

India has firmly rejected pressure from the United States regarding tariffs linked to the purchase of Russian oil, reiterating that its foreign policy decisions are guided solely by national interests. Union Minister of State for External Affairs, Kirti Vardhan Singh, addressed the issue during a recent interview, emphasizing India's independent stance on global geopolitical matters.

Singh stated that India does not make decisions based on the dictates of other countries. In response to questions about the new US sanctions legislation targeting Russian energy exports, he described the imposed tariffs as unfair. The minister stressed that the primary priority for the Indian government remains the welfare and economic security of its people, rather than aligning with external geopolitical pressures.

The US has recently introduced legislative measures aimed at penalizing countries that continue to import Russian energy products, a move intended to isolate Russia economically. India, a major buyer of discounted Russian crude, has maintained that its energy imports are driven by market dynamics and the need to keep domestic fuel prices stable. The government has consistently argued that it is a sovereign nation and will not be coerced into altering its trade policies.

This diplomatic friction highlights the complex balancing act India is performing between its strategic partnership with the US and its energy security needs. While the US seeks to tighten its sanctions net, India continues to prioritize its domestic economic stability.

What to watch: Diplomatic negotiations between New Delhi and Washington to resolve the tariff dispute without escalating tensions.
